diagrams.title: From Entered Judgment to Earned Service Fee
diagrams.subtitle: Five controlled handoffs separate enforcement authority from collected cash.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Designed for commercial post-judgment recovery. State procedure, licensing, representation requirements, and the service agreement determine permitted activity. Assignment does not automatically authorize a nonlawyer to represent another party.
diagrams.caption: Court deadlines and payment reconciliation can be automated; legal conclusions and enforcement selections remain assigned to qualified people.

stages.label: Screen the docket
stages.value: Confirm entry, parties, balance, age, and enforceability before outreach
stages.detail: Use PACER for federal matters and the relevant state court portal for state judgments. Obtain the judgment and subsequent orders; record appeals, stays, service issues, payments, and renewal deadlines with source-document links.

stages.label: Establish lawful authority
stages.value: Document creditor instructions, assignment scope, and counsel responsibilities
stages.detail: Verify the creditor and any assignment chain. Execute a service agreement defining fees, expense responsibility, remittance timing, and termination. Confirm required licenses and use counsel for reserved legal work.

stages.label: Map reachable equity
stages.value: Identify assets, competing liens, exemptions, and current bankruptcy exposure
stages.detail: Search authorized court, recorder, and Secretary of State records. Distinguish ownership from possession, subtract senior claims, and record data provenance. Do not purchase a consumer report without a documented permissible purpose.

stages.label: Select the recovery route
stages.value: Compare voluntary payment against counsel-directed execution costs and timing
stages.detail: Prepare an asset-specific cost estimate and settlement authority limits. Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 69 generally uses state execution procedure. Calendar each required notice, writ, service event, and response deadline.

stages.label: Reconcile and remit
stages.value: Allocate cleared receipts, earned fees, expenses, and creditor remittances
stages.detail: Match bank transactions to the matter ledger, investigate returns, and follow applicable client-fund handling rules. Recognize only earned operator service fees as revenue; track satisfaction filings and remaining balances.

diagrams.title: A Mature Cohort Supporting the Base Case
diagrams.subtitle: Five nested stages connect screening discipline to $280,000 in annual service fees.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative mature annual cohort, not an observed conversion benchmark or a launch-year forecast. Counts are nested: 500 >= 200 >= 100 >= 40 >= 20. Each stage is a subset of the preceding stage. First-deal planning remains 6–24 months.
diagrams.caption: Twenty collecting matters averaging $14,000 in earned fees produce $280,000 recognized revenue. At an assumed 25% fee, $1,120,000 collected for creditors underlies that revenue.

stages.label: Screened judgment records
stages.value: 500 commercial judgment records receive initial document-based screening
stages.detail: Starting cohort equals 100% of screened records. Record court identifiers, judgment dates, creditor authority, balances, and review dates without treating face value as operator revenue.

stages.label: Qualified commercial files
stages.value: 200 records satisfy documented authority, scope, and enforceability criteria
stages.detail: Forty percent of screened records survive initial review. Exclude files with unresolved authority, expired enforcement rights, unaddressed stays, or activity outside permitted scope.

stages.label: Creditor engagements
stages.value: 100 qualified files become signed, document-complete creditor engagements
stages.detail: Fifty percent of qualified files convert to engagements. Each has fee terms, expense limits, communications authority, and a defined attorney role where required.

stages.label: Actionable asset cases
stages.value: 40 engaged files support economically justified, lawful recovery action
stages.detail: Forty percent of engagements show a reachable asset or credible voluntary-payment route after priority, exemption, bankruptcy, and cost review.

stages.label: Collecting matters
stages.value: 20 actionable matters generate cleared receipts and earned service fees
stages.detail: Fifty percent of actionable cases collect within the modeled annual measurement window: 4% of initial records. Average collections of $56,000 per collecting matter at 25% yield $14,000 in recognized fees.

diagrams.title: Base Case: $280,000 Fees to $84,000 Owner Net
diagrams.subtitle: Four expense deductions reconcile exactly to a 30.0% annual net margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Annual USD. First and last bars are absolute totals; intervening bars are signed deductions. Expense allocation is illustrative; the canonical totals are $280,000 revenue, $196,000 expenses, and $84,000 owner net. Owner labor is supported by the residual rather than a second salary deduction.
diagrams.caption: $280,000 - $100,000 - $48,000 - $24,000 - $24,000 = $84,000; $84,000 / $280,000 = 30.0%. Client principal and creditor remittances never enter the revenue bar.

stages.label: Recognized service fees
stages.value: Annual earned operator fee revenue totals exactly $280,000
stages.detail: Opening total equals the canonical Base-Case revenue. Illustrative collections of $1,120,000 at a 25% service fee generate $280,000; the remaining creditor allocation is not operator revenue or an operator expense.

stages.label: Contract delivery labor
stages.value: Deduct $100,000 for nonowner research and recovery-administration delivery
stages.detail: Illustrative file-linked contractor expense covers research and administrative delivery, excluding separately budgeted outside counsel. Remaining contribution equals $180,000.

stages.label: Counsel and enforcement
stages.value: Deduct $48,000 for operator-borne legal work and execution expenses
stages.detail: Include only costs contractually borne by the operator. Do not duplicate creditor-funded advances as operator expenses. Remaining contribution equals $132,000.

stages.label: Research and systems
stages.value: Deduct $24,000 for lawful data, docket monitoring, and reconciliation systems
stages.detail: Illustrative recurring allocation equals $2,000 monthly. Maintain access permissions, source records, matter-level audit trails, and deadline alerts. Remaining contribution equals $108,000.

stages.label: Operating overhead
stages.value: Deduct $24,000 for insurance, bookkeeping, administration, and business overhead
stages.detail: Illustrative recurring allocation equals $2,000 monthly. Combined recurring systems and overhead equal $4,000 monthly, inside the $2,000–$12,000 planning range. File-linked delivery and enforcement costs remain additional.

stages.label: Annual owner net
stages.value: Closing annual owner net profit equals exactly $84,000
stages.detail: Closing total is not another cash inflow. The four-person Base pod is 1 FT + 3 C. Canonical comparison: Conservative $60,000 at 20% yields $12,000 with 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled $500,000 at 40% yields $200,000 with 2 FT + 4 C.

diagrams.title: Five Commercial File Types, One Common Collection Base
diagrams.subtitle: Compare illustrative service-fee yield per $100,000 actually recovered.
diagrams.assumptions_note: All five bars assume $100,000 in cleared recoveries and show gross operator fee yield before expenses. Rates are editorial pricing hypotheses, not observed market rates or recovery probabilities. Bars are alternatives, not additive revenue.
diagrams.caption: Use a common recovered-dollar denominator to compare pricing. Neither the debtor's asset value nor the judgment balance establishes earned revenue.

stages.label: Document-complete supplier judgments
stages.value: $100,000 recovered at 20% produces $20,000 service-fee revenue
stages.detail: Assume an entered trade-credit judgment and voluntary payment using bank-supported business ACH or wire transfer. Confirm payment authority, return exposure, and ledger allocation; a convenient rail does not improve lien priority.

stages.label: Equipment lease deficiency judgments
stages.value: $100,000 recovered at 25% produces $25,000 service-fee revenue
stages.detail: Assume a valid commercial deficiency judgment after credited disposition proceeds. Counsel reviews remaining liability and secured claims before selecting a recovery route; prevent double recovery.

stages.label: Commercial premises rent judgments
stages.value: $100,000 recovered at 25% produces $25,000 service-fee revenue
stages.detail: Confirm the named tenant entity, judgment scope, credited deposits, and any adjudicated guarantor liability. Separate commercial obligations from household-purpose debts and verify assets belong to an actual judgment debtor.

stages.label: Adjudicated business guarantor obligations
stages.value: $100,000 recovered at 30% produces $30,000 service-fee revenue
stages.detail: Assume judgment already reaches the guarantor. Classify the underlying obligation by purpose, not the person's name; counsel evaluates ownership, exemptions, and available execution procedure.

stages.label: Lien-constrained commercial judgments
stages.value: $100,000 recovered at 35% produces $35,000 service-fee revenue
stages.detail: Higher assumed pricing reflects more intensive priority and asset analysis, not superior collectability. Senior claims can eliminate reachable equity; decline further spend when incremental recovery economics fail.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Enforcement Spend
diagrams.subtitle: Proceed only on documented facts; route unresolved issues to the responsible specialist.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Read nodes in order. A supported answer advances to the next check; an unresolved or adverse answer follows the stated hold, referral, or decline path. These are jurisdiction-specific reviews, not universal procedural instructions.
diagrams.caption: A valid judgment can still be uneconomic or temporarily unenforceable. Verify authority, lawful scope, bankruptcy constraints, and net reachable value before spending.

stages.label: Authority and judgment life
stages.value: Proceed with verified enforcement rights; otherwise hold for counsel review
stages.detail: Match creditor identity, assignment documents, judgment terms, payments, appeal status, and renewal deadlines. California CCP section 683.020 illustrates the ten-year enforcement limit absent applicable renewal or exception. Federal Rule 69 generally points execution to state procedure.

stages.label: Licensing, debt purpose, and data
stages.value: Proceed within authorized scope; otherwise suspend affected research or contact
stages.detail: Check applicable state and local collection licensing even for commercial files. Apply the purpose-based debt definition in 15 U.S.C. section 1692a and Regulation F where covered. Document any consumer-report permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. section 1681b; judgment status alone does not supply one.

stages.label: Bankruptcy and protected property
stages.value: Proceed only with resolved stay exposure and an asset-specific exemption analysis
stages.detail: Refresh bankruptcy screening before enforcement. A potentially applicable 11 U.S.C. section 362 stay stops affected action pending counsel's determination or court relief. Review discharge effects under section 524, bankruptcy exemptions under section 522, and applicable state execution exemptions.

stages.label: Priority and incremental economics
stages.value: Proceed on positive expected contribution; otherwise defer or decline spending
stages.detail: Verify liens, perfection, timing, ownership, and likely sale or collection costs. State-enacted UCC section 9-317 may affect lien-creditor priority. An illustrative 40% chance of collecting $50,000 at a 25% fee produces $5,000 expected fees; subtracting $6,000 incremental operator costs produces a $1,000 expected loss.

diagrams.title: A Four-Person Base Pod, Expanded to Six
diagrams.subtitle: One owner, three contractors, and two clearly triggered expansion seats.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each node represents one person, not one full-time equivalent. Conservative and Base activate the first four seats: 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled activates all six: 2 FT + 4 C. Contractor hours and assignments vary with authorized workload.
diagrams.caption: The owner coordinates economics and client delivery; retained counsel controls legal work within the agreed representation. Separate payment preparation from release wherever feasible.

stages.label: Owner and portfolio lead
stages.value: One full-time owner leads intake, pricing, prioritization, and client accountability
stages.detail: Active in every scenario. Own engagement terms, spending limits, fee forecasts, and exception resolution. Review prepared remittances against bank evidence and matter ledgers; owner net is the scenario's residual profit.

stages.label: Lawful research contractor
stages.value: One contractor documents assets, docket facts, ownership, and competing claims
stages.detail: Active in every scenario. Use permitted public records and authorized databases, preserve source links, flag stale evidence, and escalate ambiguous identity matches. Do not select legal remedies or exceed data permissions.

stages.label: Retained enforcement attorney
stages.value: One contractor handles legal analysis, filings, and court-facing enforcement work
stages.detail: Active in every scenario, subject to the actual engagement and required jurisdictional qualifications. Determine the client and representation scope, evaluate stays and exemptions, and perform reserved legal work independently.

stages.label: Case and payment administrator
stages.value: One contractor maintains deadlines, document completeness, and receipt reconciliation
stages.detail: Active in every scenario. Maintain a shared matter register, monitor court notices, reconcile bank receipts, prepare creditor statements, and escalate missed events. Do not independently release funds that they prepared.

stages.label: Scaled operations lead
stages.value: One additional full-time employee coordinates the expanded active-file workload
stages.detail: Activate only in the Scaled six-person model. Own capacity planning, document handoffs, aging reviews, and operational quality checks while the owner retains pricing and portfolio accountability.

stages.label: Scaled data and quality contractor
stages.value: One additional contractor tests automation and independently reviews matter records
stages.detail: Activate only in the Scaled six-person model. Test deadline calculations against court rules, inspect duplicate payments and access logs, and sample lien evidence without replacing attorney review.

diagrams.title: Allocate Startup Cash Before Expanding the File Book
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets support $10,000, $30,000, and $75,000 illustrative capital plans.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values encode the $30,000 central planning stack. Bucket details also provide the $10,000 and $75,000 alternatives. Capital plans are separate from the canonical operating scenarios; startup cash is not recognized revenue or automatic annual expense.
diagrams.caption: Central allocation: $6,000 + $9,000 + $12,000 + $3,000 = $30,000. Alternative stacks total exactly $10,000 and $75,000. A 6–24 month first-deal window requires separate runway planning.

stages.label: Formation and operating readiness
stages.value: Reserve $6,000 centrally for licensing review, insurance, and engagement infrastructure
stages.detail: Allocate $2,000 in the $10,000 plan and $15,000 in the $75,000 plan: 20% throughout. Budget jurisdiction-specific license and bond costs where required, insurance, entity setup, and counsel-reviewed service documents.

stages.label: Research and workflow systems
stages.value: Reserve $9,000 centrally for lawful data access and dependable case systems
stages.detail: Allocate $3,000 in the $10,000 plan and $22,500 in the $75,000 plan: 30% throughout. Fund authorized record retrieval, docket tracking, secure document storage, access controls, and payment-ledger setup.

stages.label: Enforcement working cash
stages.value: Reserve $12,000 centrally for approved operator-borne file costs and delivery
stages.detail: Allocate $4,000 in the $10,000 plan and $30,000 in the $75,000 plan: 40% throughout. Release cash against matter-level budgets for counsel, filing, service, and contractor delivery. Track creditor advances separately.

stages.label: Liquidity and error reserve
stages.value: Reserve $3,000 centrally for payment interruptions, corrections, and operating contingencies
stages.detail: Allocate $1,000 in the $10,000 plan and $7,500 in the $75,000 plan: 10% throughout. This is not full launch runway: 6 months at $2,000 monthly consumes $12,000, while 24 months at $12,000 consumes $288,000.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to an Auditable Recovery Operation
diagrams.subtitle: Four weekly milestones establish readiness without assuming first-month collections.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The sprint establishes operating capability, not a collection deadline. Canonical time to first deal remains 6–24 months. Training files and synthetic payment records stay separate from authorized live matters.
diagrams.caption: Finish the month with documented scope, a screened file queue, tested controls, and a funded operating plan. Do not book judgment principal, prospective recoveries, or unsigned fees as revenue.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Define jurisdiction, commercial scope, representation roles, and operating economics
stages.detail: Select one initial jurisdiction and commercial file type. Document licensing research, counsel responsibilities, lawful data sources, fee terms, and expense ownership. Load canonical revenue, margin, and staffing scenarios into a spreadsheet without changing their totals.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Build the source-linked screening register and test deadline ownership
stages.detail: Review 25 lawfully accessible judgment records as an internal process sample, not a sales forecast. Capture entry dates, balances, authority evidence, relevant orders, and review decisions. Have counsel verify jurisdiction-specific deadline logic.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Exercise bankruptcy checks, priority review, and payment-allocation controls
stages.detail: Run five training cases through the four pre-flight checks. Test synthetic partial payments, duplicate receipts, reversals, creditor advances, and fee splits. Confirm that deadline alerts reach a named owner and that system failures produce visible exceptions.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Launch bounded creditor outreach and review readiness, capacity, and runway
stages.detail: Contact an initial list of ten prospective commercial creditor organizations using permitted business channels. Accept live work only within established authority and capacity. Review cash runway, contractor commitments, record completeness, and unresolved legal questions before committing matter-specific expenditure.
